relationship_types.definition: Scopes a category assignment to one target set.

relationship_types.label: characterisation relative to objective
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the objective relative to which a target characterisation was assessed.
relationship_types.review_boundary: This relation supplies assessment context; it does not assert causal support for the objective or imply priority, validation or authority.

relationship_types.label: compares with baseline
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the governed baseline used by an assessment.

relationship_types.label: identifies underlying component entity
relationship_types.definition: Links a contextual target-system-component record to its underlying entity.

relationship_types.label: component contributes to function
relationship_types.definition: Records the system function to which a contextual component contributes.

relationship_types.label: component within target system
relationship_types.definition: Scopes a component assignment to one target system.

relationship_types.label: identifies critical entity or element
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the element or entity assessed as critical.

relationship_types.label: critical for function
relationship_types.definition: Records the function for which an element is assessed as critical.

relationship_types.label: critical within target system
relationship_types.definition: Scopes a critical-element assessment to one target system.

relationship_types.label: criticality assessed for objective
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the objective context for which an element's criticality was assessed.
relationship_types.review_boundary: This relation scopes a judgement; it does not assert that the element causally supports the objective or infer lawfulness, priority or engageability.

relationship_types.label: dependency has alternative
relationship_types.definition: Records an assessed alternative provider or mechanism for a dependency.

relationship_types.label: dependency has failure consequence
relationship_types.definition: Links a dependency to an assessment of the consequences of its loss or degradation.

relationship_types.label: dependency provider
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the provider in a qualified dependency record.

relationship_types.label: dependency subject
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the dependent subject in a qualified dependency record.

relationship_types.label: dependency supports function
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the function sustained by a dependency.

relationship_types.label: identifies underlying target element
relationship_types.definition: Links a contextual target-element record to its underlying entity or feature.

relationship_types.label: element enables function
relationship_types.definition: Records the target function enabled by an element.

relationship_types.label: element of designation
relationship_types.definition: Scopes a target element to a contextual target designation.

relationship_types.label: expresses commander's intent
relationship_types.definition: Links guidance or a plan to the versioned commander's intent statement it expresses.

relationship_types.label: flow uses interface
relationship_types.definition: Binds a qualified input, output or flow to the interface through which it passes.

relationship_types.label: follows joint targeting cycle
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the governed cycle definition used by an iteration.

relationship_types.label: grant creates authority-holder state
relationship_types.definition: Links an authority-grant event to the time-bounded holder state it establishes.
surface_forms: authority holder state created by grant
relationship_types.inverse_reading: authority holder state created by grant
relationship_types.review_boundary: The state must remain distinct from the grant event and normative permission and must use core_rel:validDuring.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required when the grant takes effect

relationship_types.label: grant records target engagement authority
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the normative scoped permission created or delegated by an authority-grant record.
surface_forms: target engagement authority recorded by grant
relationship_types.inverse_reading: target engagement authority recorded by grant
relationship_types.review_boundary: This relation records an authorised grant; asserting it in the graph cannot create, delegate or exercise authority.

relationship_types.label: has allocation assignment
relationship_types.definition: Links a list-membership record to an authoritative component allocation.

relationship_types.label: has assessment level
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one analytic scope from vocab:AssessmentLevel to a relevant targeting assessment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The object must be a concept in vocab:AssessmentLevel. Level denotes analytic scope; it does not establish causal hierarchy, certainty or completion.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required where an assessment level is applicable

relationship_types.label: has battle damage assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links an action, event or designation to a battle damage assessment.

relationship_types.label: has collateral damage assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links an action or event to a retrospective collateral damage assessment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: A retrospective assessment must not overwrite or be confused with the earlier estimate.

relationship_types.label: has collateral damage estimate
relationship_types.definition: Links a planned action to a prospective collateral damage estimate produced by the applicable authorised process.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The profile may represent an authorised estimate but cannot calculate, generate or approve one. A prospective estimate is not an observation or retrospective assessment.

relationship_types.label: has decision disposition
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one result from vocab:DecisionDisposition to a targeting decision record.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The object must be a concept in vocab:DecisionDisposition. A disposition applies only to the cited decision and does not merge validation, nomination, approval, legal review or authority.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required on each completed targeting decision

relationship_types.label: has development-standard assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a target-development case to one assessment of a named standard.

relationship_types.label: has development-standard outcome
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one result from vocab:DevelopmentStandardOutcome to a target-development-standard assessment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The object must be a concept in vocab:DevelopmentStandardOutcome. It is a human assessment result, not model confidence or automatic stage promotion.

relationship_types.label: has functional damage assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a battle damage assessment to its functional finding.
surface_forms: functional assessment part of battle damage assessment
relationship_types.inverse_reading: functional assessment part of battle damage assessment

relationship_types.label: has input
relationship_types.definition: Links a subject to a qualified input role or record.

relationship_types.label: has interface
relationship_types.definition: Links a governed subject to a qualified interface record.

relationship_types.label: has output
relationship_types.definition: Links a subject to a qualified output role or record.

relationship_types.label: has physical damage assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a battle damage assessment to its physical finding.
surface_forms: physical assessment part of battle damage assessment
relationship_types.inverse_reading: physical assessment part of battle damage assessment

relationship_types.label: has positive-identification assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a designation or target-development case to a time-bounded positive-identification assessment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Positive identification does not establish identity equivalence, validation, legal status or approval; a planned action is context, not the assessed subject.

relationship_types.label: has positive-identification outcome
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one result from vocab:PositiveIdentificationOutcome to a positive-identification assessment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The object must be a concept in vocab:PositiveIdentificationOutcome. The result is not entity resolution, validation, legal approval or engagement authority.

relationship_types.label: has priority assignment
relationship_types.definition: Links a nomination or membership to its time-bounded priority record.

relationship_types.label: has priority value
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one authority-governed machine-readable value from vocab:TargetPriorityValue, or a registered local extension of that scheme, to a priority assignment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: No universal ranking scale is asserted. Preserve the exact authority-governed code and scheme; do not derive priority from graph centrality or model score.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required when a priority assignment states a value

relationship_types.label: has reconstitution assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a subject to an assessment of restoration after loss or degradation.

relationship_types.label: has residual capability assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a subject to an assessment of remaining capability.

relationship_types.label: has system resilience assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a system, function or capability to a scenario-specific resilience assessment.

relationship_types.label: has target-category assignment
relationship_types.definition: Links a contextual target designation to a category assignment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Category is a targeting judgement about the designation in context, not an intrinsic class of the underlying entity.

relationship_types.label: has target characterisation
relationship_types.definition: Links a contextual target designation to one explicit characterisation assignment.

relationship_types.label: has target system assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a battle damage assessment to its target-system finding.
surface_forms: system assessment part of battle damage assessment
relationship_types.inverse_reading: system assessment part of battle damage assessment

relationship_types.label: has target system model
relationship_types.definition: Links a report to the versioned target system model it presents.
surface_forms: model in target system analysis report
relationship_types.inverse_reading: model in target system analysis report

relationship_types.label: has targeting-cycle iteration
relationship_types.definition: Links an operation or plan to one period-scoped targeting-cycle iteration.

relationship_types.label: has targeting guidance
relationship_types.definition: Links a governed context to the applicable version of targeting guidance.

relationship_types.label: has targeting-mode assignment
relationship_types.definition: Links a cycle iteration, phase activity, planned action or explicitly phase-scoped case to a contextual targeting-mode assignment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Mode is contextual and time-bounded. If assigned to a development case, record the applicable phase/activity and valid interval; never make mode an enduring characteristic of the entity.

relationship_types.label: has targeting-phase activity
relationship_types.definition: Links a cycle iteration to an activity assigned to one targeting phase.

relationship_types.label: holder state for target engagement authority
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the normative permission held during an authority-holder state.
surface_forms: holder state for target engagement authority
target engagement authority held in state
relationship_types.inverse_reading: target engagement authority held in state
relationship_types.review_boundary: Holding one permission does not imply any broader authority; record supersession, withdrawal and expiry explicitly.

relationship_types.label: implements targeting guidance
relationship_types.definition: Links a task, decision or nomination to the guidance it implements.

relationship_types.label: input supplied by
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the supplier of a qualified input.

relationship_types.label: interface connects to
relationship_types.definition: Identifies an endpoint represented by an interface record when the source does not state a directional role.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Use the provider and consumer endpoint relationships whenever the source supplies direction; do not infer direction from this neutral endpoint relation.

relationship_types.label: interface consumer endpoint
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the consumer or downstream endpoint of a qualified interface.

relationship_types.label: interface provider endpoint
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the provider or upstream endpoint of a qualified interface.

relationship_types.label: material for target case
relationship_types.definition: Links target material to the development case it supports.

relationship_types.label: output consumed by
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the consumer of a qualified output.

relationship_types.label: positive identification recognises function
relationship_types.definition: Records the functional component of a positive-identification assessment.

relationship_types.label: positive identification recognises location
relationship_types.definition: Records the locational component of a positive-identification assessment.

relationship_types.label: priority assigned for objective
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the objective for which a priority was assigned.
surface_forms: objective for which priority was assigned
relationship_types.inverse_reading: objective for which priority was assigned
relationship_types.review_boundary: This relation records assignment context; it does not assert that the target or priority causally supports the objective.

relationship_types.label: report documents assessment
relationship_types.definition: Links a versioned targeting-assessment report to each distinct assessment or finding it documents.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The report must preserve the assessment identifier, model or method version, generating activity, evidence, provenance and unresolved contradiction; documentation does not merge distinct assessment levels.

relationship_types.label: represents target system
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the target system represented by a model version.

relationship_types.label: standard assessment for designation
relationship_types.definition: Scopes a development-standard assessment to a contextual designation.

relationship_types.label: target engagement authority applies to
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the designation, entity, planned action, target system, target set or capability within the explicit scope of a target-engagement-authority specification.
surface_forms: within scope of target engagement authority
relationship_types.inverse_reading: within scope of target engagement authority
relationship_types.review_boundary: Scope is closed only where the governing instrument says so; no authority beyond the recorded scope may be inferred.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required on each target engagement authority

relationship_types.label: uses target selection standards
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the exact standards version used by an assessment.

relationship_types.label: assessment subject
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the entity, action, event, function, capability, objective or target system evaluated by a targeting assessment.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required on each concrete targeting assessment
relationship_types.review_boundary: An assessment subject may be proposed for review only when supported by an exact source span; it is not an engagement recommendation.

relationship_types.label: assessment has finding
relationship_types.definition: Links a targeting assessment to a qualified finding represented as an assertion, effect, state or controlled value.
relationship_types.requiredness: Required when an assessment states a finding
relationship_types.review_boundary: Preserve the stated qualitative or quantitative finding, unit, qualifier, baseline, uncertainty and evidence; do not invent missing values.

relationship_types.label: target-type assignment has value
relationship_types.definition: Assigns one FIVE-O target-type concept to a contextual target-type assignment; it does not determine lawfulness or permanent identity.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Extract only an explicit contextual FIVE-O assignment; do not infer it from a name, occupation, location or legal status.

relationship_types.label: development-stage assignment has value
relationship_types.definition: Assigns the explicitly recorded basic, intermediate or advanced stage to a time-bounded target-development-stage assignment.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Do not infer stage from apparent completeness or automatically promote a case; preserve the recorded decision and effective time.

relationship_types.label: target list has type
relationship_types.definition: Assigns the declared NATO target-list type to a versioned target list; membership and membership authority remain separate records.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Use only an explicit list type or governed acronym; never infer list membership, approval, restriction or authority from the list type.

relationship_types.label: resolution case has candidate
relationship_types.definition: Links an entity-resolution case to a candidate record without asserting that the records denote the same entity.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Candidate inclusion is reversible and does not merge records or establish identity.

relationship_types.label: resolution case uses feature
relationship_types.definition: Records the feature or governed feature set used by an entity-resolution case for reproducibility and leakage review.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Record feature provenance and version; a feature score is not an identity decision.

relationship_types.label: resolution decision for case
relationship_types.definition: Links a human-reviewed resolution decision to the resolution case it decides.
relationship_types.review_boundary: The model may extract the recorded decision-case link but cannot make the decision.

relationship_types.label: resolution decision has outcome
relationship_types.definition: Assigns the recorded controlled outcome to a human-reviewed entity-resolution decision.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Never derive this outcome from a similarity score; retain the decision maker, time, evidence and alternatives.

relationship_types.label: resolution decision made by
relationship_types.definition: Identifies the accountable agent or authority that made a recorded resolution decision.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Do not infer the decision maker from authorship, system ownership or model execution.

relationship_types.label: fusion decision has input
relationship_types.definition: Links a reviewed fusion decision to each retained assertion or assertion cluster used as input.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Retain every input and its provenance, including contradictory or superseded records.

relationship_types.label: fusion decision produces reviewed view
relationship_types.definition: Links a reviewed fusion decision to the resulting assertion cluster or reviewed current view without deleting its inputs.
relationship_types.inverse_reading: reviewed view produced by fusion decision
relationship_types.review_boundary: The output remains traceable to all contributing assertions and does not overwrite source records.

relationship_types.label: assertion has subject
relationship_types.definition: Subject component of a reified assertion created by the host projection from a grounded relationship extraction.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created by the host from validated subject fields; never emitted as an additional model relationship.

relationship_types.label: assertion has predicate
relationship_types.definition: Predicate component of a reified assertion created by the host projection from a validated canonical relationship ID.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created by the host from the validated predicate_id; never emitted as an additional model relationship.

relationship_types.label: assertion has object
relationship_types.definition: Object component of a reified assertion created by the host projection while preserving entity-resolution and literal-value state.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created by the host from validated object fields; never collapses an unresolved mention into an entity.

relationship_types.label: assertion has polarity
relationship_types.definition: Assigns the validated polarity token to a reified assertion during host graph projection.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created by the host from the validated polarity attribute; unknown is never converted to negative.

relationship_types.label: assertion has modality
relationship_types.definition: Assigns the validated evidential or production modality to a reified assertion during host graph projection.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created by the host from the validated modality attribute; it does not establish authority or truth.

relationship_types.label: assertion cluster has member
relationship_types.definition: Links a reviewed assertion cluster to each retained member assertion without deleting contradictory or superseded records.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Created from a reviewed fusion record; never inferred from textual similarity alone.

relationship_types.label: event occurs at time
relationship_types.definition: Records the explicitly stated occurrence time of an event or activity as a time instant, distinct from observation, reporting and validity times.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Do not substitute document, report or observation time for event occurrence time.

relationship_types.label: event occurs during
relationship_types.definition: Records the explicitly stated occurrence interval of an event or activity, distinct from observation, reporting and record-validity intervals.
relationship_types.review_boundary: Do not substitute document, report or observation time for event occurrence interval.

relationship_types.label: states objective
relationship_types.definition: Links targeting guidance, a commander's intent statement or a plan to an explicitly stated operation-scoped objective.
relationship_types.inverse_reading: objective stated by guidance or plan
relationship_types.review_boundary: Extract only the explicit objective and its governing context; do not convert an analytic recommendation into command intent.

relationship_types.label: states constraint
relationship_types.definition: Links targeting guidance, a commander's intent statement or a plan to an explicitly stated externally imposed limitation.
relationship_types.inverse_reading: constraint stated by guidance or plan
relationship_types.review_boundary: Do not infer a constraint from preference, feasibility or model policy; retain the issuing authority and effective time.

relationship_types.label: states restraint
relationship_types.definition: Links targeting guidance, a commander's intent statement or a plan to an explicitly stated internally chosen limitation.
relationship_types.inverse_reading: restraint stated by guidance or plan
relationship_types.review_boundary: Keep restraint distinct from external constraint and list restriction; retain authority and effective time.

value_sets.label: Joint targeting cycle phase
value_sets.definition: Named phase in the six-phase joint targeting cycle; phases may overlap, repeat or return to an earlier phase.

values.label: Commander's intent, objectives and targeting guidance
values.definition: Phase 1: establish commander's intent, objectives and targeting guidance.

values.label: Target development
values.definition: Phase 2: conduct target development.

values.label: Capabilities analysis
values.definition: Phase 3: conduct capabilities analysis.

values.label: Commander's decision, force planning and assignment
values.definition: Phase 4: record commander's decision, force planning and assignment.

values.label: Mission planning and force execution
values.definition: Phase 5: conduct mission planning and force execution.

values.label: Assessment
values.definition: Phase 6: conduct assessment and feed findings back into the cycle.

value_sets.governance_note: Phases may iterate and overlap; sequence numbers are labels, not automatic transitions.

value_sets.label: Targeting mode
value_sets.definition: Mode assigned to a targeting activity under the applicable guidance.

values.label: Deliberate
values.definition: Targeting mode for anticipated targets processed with sufficient planning time.

values.label: Dynamic
values.definition: Targeting mode for targets identified too late, or not selected, for deliberate processing under the applicable guidance.

value_sets.governance_note: Mode applies to a case or activity, never intrinsically to the entity.

value_sets.label: Basic target-development standard
value_sets.definition: One of the five basic target-development standards used to assess identification, location, function, significance and description.

values.label: Identification
values.definition: Basic target-development standard concerning identification of the entity or designation.

values.label: Location
values.definition: Basic target-development standard concerning the target's location.

values.label: Function
values.definition: Basic target-development standard concerning the target's function.

values.label: Significance
values.definition: Basic target-development standard concerning significance in context.

values.label: Description
values.definition: Basic target-development standard concerning sufficient description.

value_sets.governance_note: Assess each standard separately and preserve missing or unresolved findings.

value_sets.label: Development-standard outcome
value_sets.definition: Outcome of an assessment against one named target-development standard.

values.label: Not assessed
values.definition: The named development standard has not been assessed.

values.label: Insufficient
values.definition: Available evidence is insufficient to meet the named development standard.

values.label: Partial
values.definition: The named development standard is only partly met.

values.label: Met
values.definition: The named development standard is recorded as met.

values.label: Not applicable
values.definition: The named development standard is not applicable in the governed context.

values.label: Cannot be judged
values.definition: The named development standard cannot be judged from available information.

value_sets.governance_note: An outcome is a human assessment result and never a model confidence score.

value_sets.label: Positive-identification outcome
value_sets.definition: Recorded outcome of a time-bounded positive-identification assessment.

values.label: Not assessed
values.definition: Positive identification has not been assessed.

values.label: Not established
values.definition: Positive identification is recorded as not established.

values.label: Established
values.definition: Positive identification is recorded as established for the stated function, location and period.

values.label: No longer current
values.definition: A previously established positive-identification assessment is no longer current.

values.label: Cannot be judged
values.definition: Positive identification cannot be judged from available information.

value_sets.governance_note: The finding is time-bounded and distinct from entity resolution, validation and legal approval.

value_sets.label: Target characterisation
value_sets.definition: Context- and time-bounded target characterisation; no value in this scheme is an intrinsic entity type.

values.label: Sensitive target
values.definition: Target explicitly designated as requiring strategic or national review or approval under applicable guidance.

values.label: Time-sensitive target
values.definition: Target explicitly designated as requiring immediate response because it poses, or will soon pose, a danger or is a highly lucrative fleeting opportunity, and therefore cannot be processed within the normal targeting timeline.

values.label: High-value target
values.definition: Target assessed as critical to an identified actor or organisation for achieving a stated goal or executing a course of action in context.

values.label: High-pay-off target
values.definition: High-value target assessed to offer disproportionate advantage to friendly action in context.

values.label: Component-critical target
values.definition: Target explicitly designated by a component command as requiring immediate response and carrying high tactical priority in support of its assigned objective.

value_sets.governance_note: Restricted-target and no-strike status use separate restriction, protection and list-membership records.

value_sets.label: Targeting assessment level
value_sets.definition: Level at which a targeting assessment reports its finding.

values.label: Physical
values.definition: Assessment level concerning physical condition or change.

values.label: Functional
values.definition: Assessment level concerning ability to perform a function.

values.label: Target system
values.definition: Assessment level concerning consequences across a target system.

values.label: Operational
values.definition: Assessment level concerning operational effects or progress.

values.label: Campaign
values.definition: Assessment level concerning campaign-level effects or progress.

value_sets.governance_note: Levels identify analytic scope and do not imply causal hierarchy.

value_sets.label: Target-priority value
value_sets.definition: Operation-specific target-priority value governed by the applicable versioned authority or guidance.
value_sets.open_value_policy: Retain the exact source value and governing-guidance reference; route it for human normalisation and do not invent a closed code list.
value_sets.governance_note: Open authority-governed scheme. Load the exact codes and ordering from the applicable versioned guidance or list; this profile asserts no universal numeric or qualitative priority scale.

value_sets.label: Targeting decision disposition
value_sets.definition: Disposition explicitly recorded by an authorised targeting decision.

values.label: Approved
values.definition: The authorised decision records approval.

values.label: Approved with conditions
values.definition: The authorised decision records approval subject to stated conditions.

values.label: Rejected
values.definition: The authorised decision records rejection.

values.label: Deferred
values.definition: The authorised decision records deferral.

values.label: Referred
values.definition: The authorised decision records referral to another authority or forum.

values.label: Withdrawn
values.definition: The authorised decision records withdrawal.

values.label: Superseded
values.definition: The authorised decision has been replaced by a later governed decision.

value_sets.governance_note: Every value needs an authorised decision, rationale, effective period and evidence.

value_sets.label: FIVE-O target type
value_sets.definition: Doctrinal target-type values applied to a contextual target designation, not to permanent identity or lawfulness.

values.label: Facility
values.definition: A fixed installation, structure or geographically bounded facility treated as a contextual target type.

values.label: Individual
values.definition: A named or otherwise identified person treated as a contextual target type.

values.label: Virtual entity
values.definition: A non-physical information, software, data or cyberspace entity treated as a contextual target type.

values.label: Equipment
values.definition: A movable physical item or equipment system treated as a contextual target type.

values.label: Organisation
values.definition: An organisation or organised group treated as a contextual target type.

value_sets.governance_note: US target-development interoperability extension. Verify values and usage against an authorised copy of CJCSI 3370.01C before operational use; do not present this scheme as UK/NATO doctrine.

value_sets.label: NATO target-list type
value_sets.definition: NATO target-list type; each list has a distinct purpose and authority-scoped membership decision.

values.label: Candidate target list
values.definition: A list of entities in target development that have not yet been validated; admission is not validation or approval.

values.label: Joint target list
values.definition: A list of validated targets that have not yet been approved for the joint prioritised target list.

values.label: Restricted target list
values.definition: A JTL subset of targets restricted by the joint force commander or higher authority; restriction scope, authority and time remain separate records.

values.label: Target nomination list
values.definition: A prioritised list of nominations forwarded to the Joint Targeting Coordination Board for consideration for the joint prioritised target list.

values.label: Joint prioritised target list
values.definition: The joint-force-commander-approved and maintained list that constitutes formal tasking to component commands for the applicable period.

values.label: Prioritised target list
values.definition: A list derived from the joint prioritised target list that allocates prioritised targets to component commands for the applicable period.

values.label: No-strike list
values.definition: A list of protected or restricted entities for which the governing legal or policy rationale and authority must be recorded separately.

value_sets.governance_note: NSL is modelled under AdministrativeList to accommodate US divergence; list rules remain profile-specific.

value_sets.label: Target-development stage
value_sets.definition: Target-development stage recorded by a dated assignment; stages do not replace quality-control or validation decisions.

values.label: Basic target development
values.definition: Begins unique identification, location, description, functional characterisation and databasing against the identification, location, function, significance and description standards; it does not imply validation or approval.

values.label: Intermediate target development
values.definition: Provides sufficient intelligence to complete functional characterisation and qualify a candidate for validation to the JTL or RTL, including system-impact and adversary-mitigation analysis; assignment must be explicit.

values.label: Advanced target development
values.definition: Completes target characterisation and defines the minimum intelligence for effective engagement planning, including capability-specific mission data; it does not itself confer authority.

value_sets.governance_note: NATO target-development stages grounded in AJP-3.9. CJCSI 3370.01C is retained only as a US interoperability cross-reference and must be verified against an authorised copy before claiming US conformance.

value_sets.label: Assertion modality
value_sets.definition: How the proposition was obtained or expressed; modality does not by itself establish truth, authority or acceptance.

values.label: Observed
values.definition: Directly observed in the cited evidence; observation time and observer should be retained when stated.

values.label: Reported
values.definition: Reported by the cited source without adopting the proposition as independently observed or accepted.

values.label: Quoted
values.definition: Presented as a quotation attributed to another speaker or document.

values.label: Analyst assessed
values.definition: Expressed as a human analytic judgement with its assessor, evidence, uncertainty and time retained where stated.

values.label: Deterministically derived
values.definition: Produced by a reproducible deterministic rule from retained inputs; not source-reported fact.

values.label: Model predicted
values.definition: Produced by a model and retained as a prediction with immutable model-run provenance; not an observation or accepted assertion.

values.label: Hypothesised
values.definition: Proposed as a hypothesis for testing rather than asserted as established fact.

value_sets.governance_note: Does not imply truth or approval.

value_sets.label: Assertion polarity
value_sets.definition: Whether the proposition is stated positively, negated, unknown or mixed; unknown is not false.

values.label: Positive
values.definition: The proposition is explicitly affirmed by the source under its stated modality and certainty.

values.label: Negated
values.definition: The source explicitly negates the proposition; preserve the scope of negation.

values.label: Unknown
values.definition: The source explicitly records that the proposition is not known or cannot be determined.

values.label: Mixed
values.definition: The source contains qualified or conflicting positive and negative content that must be retained rather than collapsed.

value_sets.governance_note: Negation is preserved; absence of a positive assertion is not negation.

value_sets.label: Entity-resolution outcome
value_sets.definition: Reversible outcome explicitly recorded by a human-reviewed entity-resolution decision.

values.label: Possible match
values.definition: The candidates may denote the same entity, but no identity merge is authorised.

values.label: Confirmed same
values.definition: The accountable resolution decision records that the candidates denote the same entity; contributing records and provenance are retained.

values.label: Confirmed distinct
values.definition: The accountable resolution decision records that the candidates denote different entities.

values.label: Merged
values.definition: A governed fusion or resolution process created a shared reviewed view while retaining source records and decision provenance.

values.label: Split
values.definition: A governed decision separated a previously combined record into distinct entity views with provenance retained.

values.label: Deferred
values.definition: The resolution decision is deferred pending further evidence or review; candidates remain distinct.

value_sets.governance_note: A decision record and reversible audit event are required.

state_dimensions.label: Joint-targeting-cycle phase
state_dimensions.note: Activities may overlap, repeat or return to an earlier phase. A phase number is not a workflow-transition rule.

state_dimensions.label: Target-development stage
state_dimensions.note: A later assignment does not erase earlier evidence or guarantee that every standard remains current.

state_dimensions.label: Assurance decisions
state_dimensions.note: Quality control is intelligence-led and target validation is operations-led. Neither implies legal approval or engagement authority.

state_dimensions.label: Target-list membership
state_dimensions.note: CATL, JTL, RTL, TNL, JPTL, PTL and NSL are list identities, not a universal single-state sequence.

state_dimensions.label: Contextual target characterisation
state_dimensions.note: Sensitive, time-sensitive, high-value, high-pay-off and component-critical are not intrinsic entity classes.

state_dimensions.label: Assessment level and reassessment
state_dimensions.note: TargetingAssessment is an abstract organising type. Instantiate a declared concrete assessment class; keep physical, functional and target-system findings distinct and reassess as evidence changes.

distinction_rules.rule: The enduring thing remains separate from the operation-scoped designation.
A system is a geographically situated functional grouping; a set is an approved functional grouping under the cited profile.
IES System is a hardware/software device; a NATO target system must not be exact-mapped to it.
The first is a contextual role in a target system; the second is a structural part.
An element enables a function; criticality is a separate assessment.
FIVE-O classifies a designation; a category groups by function or analytic purpose.
BTD, ITD and ATD are development stages or steps and remain separate from review status.
Quality control is intelligence-led; validation is operations-led under delegated authority.
A valid designation is not automatically nominated, prioritised, allocated or approved.
Each list has a distinct purpose and membership decision; no list is an intrinsic entity type.
Restriction, sensitivity and urgency are different contextual judgements.
These are separately scoped authorities and must not be inferred from each other.
Positive identification is function- and location-based in context; entity resolution assesses identity across records.
The first is prospective; the second is retrospective.
Observed physical change does not establish functional or system consequence.
Plans and models are not observations and remain in separate assertion layers.
The first concerns task execution; the second concerns achieved effects or objectives.

validation_rules.statement: Every target designation identifies an underlying entity or area, operation context, validity interval, doctrine profile and evidence.
The underlying entity is never typed as a target, sensitive target, restricted target or time-sensitive target.
FIVE-O applies to the target designation and not directly to the underlying entity.
Every basic-development case assesses identification, location, function, significance and description separately.
Development stages are dated assignments; later stages do not overwrite earlier stages.
Assignment of the intermediate-development stage requires functional characterisation, system-impact analysis and mitigation analysis.
Quality control is intelligence-led and remains distinct from operations-led validation.

Target validation has two doctrinal steps: determine that a potential target is a valid target, then place it on the joint target list or restricted target list; represent the determination and resulting membership as distinct, linked audit records.

Candidate target list admission requires the applicable target-development and quality-control standards to be recorded as met, or an explicit authorised exception; CATL membership does not imply target validation or approval.
Joint or restricted target list membership requires an accepted validation decision.
Target nomination does not imply validation, approval or list placement.
Joint prioritised target list membership requires an authoritative approval decision and effective period.
Prioritised target list membership or allocation traces to a joint prioritised target list record.
Restricted target list membership has a restriction specifying scope, duration and who may lift it.
No-strike list membership has a legal or policy rationale, responsible authority and effective interval.
No model may infer that protected status has ended or that a no-strike entity may be removed.
Sensitive, time-sensitive, high-value and high-pay-off characterisations remain distinct.
A high-pay-off characterisation has an explicit high-value basis and is not inferred from graph centrality.
Positive identification records function, location, observation time, criteria, sources and confidence.
Positive identification is not entity resolution and does not replace legal or validation review.
Target selection standards identify their version, context, authority and criteria.
Target-system membership identifies the underlying entity, system, function, context, interval and evidence.
Target-system component is not the same as a structural engineering component.
A critical-element designation identifies the element, function, target system, objective, context, interval and evidence.
A dependency record identifies the dependent, provider, supported function, direction, time and evidence.
Dependency, support and causal relationships are not transitively materialised.
Target system, target set and IES System remain semantically distinct.
The profile may represent an authorised prospective collateral damage estimate but cannot calculate, generate or approve one; retrospective collateral damage assessment remains separate.
Battle damage assessment keeps physical, functional and target-system findings distinct.
Absence of observed physical damage does not establish absence of functional or target-system effects.
Intended, predicted, assessed and observed effects remain separate assertions.
First-, second- and higher-order effects are assessed categories and not graph-hop counts.
Measures of performance concern task accomplishment; measures of effectiveness concern effects, objectives or end state.
Validation authority, target engagement authority, legal advice and national approval remain separate.
An inverse reading is never emitted as a second source assertion.
The model cannot validate, approve, lift restrictions, remove protection or assign target engagement authority.
The profile cannot select capabilities, recommend engagement or represent an automated use-of-force decision.
Training examples use fictional or sanitised content and exclude actionable coordinates, methods and protected operational data.
Vetting is not a NATO-core stage in this profile; any national vetting extension needs an identified national authority and source.
Every profile relationship uses canonical subject-to-object direction and retains its exact source evidence.

Target engagement authority is a normative scoped permission; its grant or delegation and holder state are distinct linked records identifying grantor, grantee or holder, governing instrument, scope, valid interval and evidence.

An accepted Target Set records the applicable approval identified by the governing doctrine profile; in the AJP-3.9 NATO profile this is North Atlantic Council approval. An unapproved analytic grouping remains a candidate grouping, target system or target category.

Joint prioritised target list membership records Joint Force Commander-approved authoritative tasking in the AJP-3.9 context; it does not prove engagement, legal permissibility, successful prosecution or a standalone grant of target engagement authority.
A sensitive-target characterisation records the applicable strategic or national review or approval requirement, authority, context and effective period.

A time-sensitive-target characterisation records the explicit commander or joint-task-force designation, immediacy criteria and operational period; urgency is not inferred from age, centrality or reporting volume.

A high-value-target characterisation records criticality to an identified actor or organisation for achieving a stated goal or executing a course of action; it is not inferred from generic importance.
A high-pay-off-target characterisation records its high-value basis and the assessed disproportionate advantage to friendly action.
A component-critical-target characterisation records the component commander's decision and the immediate-response or tactical-objective context.
